messages:
maria (Support): FYI escalated from account team — multiple customers seeing 502s on hosted API when doing streaming responses. Spike started ~2026-03-05T02:12:xxZ. Primary repro from Customer A: h2 streaming session, long response (>1.5MB), intermittent 502 with upstream reset. Trace IDs attached.

raj (Eng-SRE): thanks — can you paste an example trace id and last_request headers? also did they report any auth changes or deploys around that time?

maria (Support): trace: trace-20260305-1a2b3c, customer says they rotated their service token earlier that day (rolling rotation). No explicit deploy on our side in the 2h window per alerts, but there was an autoscaler event at 02:10:03 UTC.

logan (DevEx): ping @taylor — any known h2 regressions? we had that keepalive tweak last month but shouldn't impact streaming that much.

ops-bot: Deployment check: no user-facing deploys between 2026-03-05T00:00:00Z and 2026-03-05T04:00:00Z.

raj (Eng-SRE): looking at edge logs for trace-20260305-1a2b3c — envoy shows upstream reset: 
```
[2026-03-05T02:12:17.123Z] "POST /v1/generate" 502 response_code:502 upstream_response_time:0.005 upstream_reset: BEFORE_RESPONSE upstream_host:10.4.27.91
```
Not a full upstream 5xx, looks like upstream closed the h2 stream. Window underrun? Also seeing many connections with GOAWAY from upstream hosts at the same time.

maria (Support): customer provided a curl repro (they recommended http2):
```
curl -v --http2 -H "Authorization: Bearer <rotated-token>" -d @long_prompt.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
They say successful often, but ~1/10 attempts return 502 mid-stream.

logan (DevEx): can you try with a pre-rotation token vs rotated token to reproduce locally? maybe token length/headers cause different header compression behaviour.

maria (Support): tried locally w/ old token and new token, both repro but higher probability with new token.

raj (Eng-SRE): note: at 02:10 we had a brief spike of upstream pod restarts in hosted-model-pool-us-east-1, likely due to autoscaler reacting to burst. Pod churn + h2 long-lived streams = possible stream collisions and GOAWAY propagation. If client retries quickly with same connection that got GOAWAY, envoy may return 502.

taylor (Eng-Runtime): adding runtime context: our model-serving instances currently accept long lived h2 connections and reuse them aggressively. We also added recent change to auth middleware that inspects JWTs earlier in the request lifecycle (to improve rate accounting). That middleware touched header processing path — if a pod restarts mid-validate we could see upstream reset.

maria (Support): customer reports this happens more often when their prompt produces very long outputs (streaming many tokens).

raj (Eng-SRE): reproduction steps I'm running: 1) start a looped curl with http2, large prompt, 2) trigger a pod restart in backend pool, 3) observe 502s on client that didn't reconnect. Example script:
```
for i in {1..100}; do 
  curl --http2 -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @big.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate || echo "fail $i"; 
  sleep 0.2; 
done
```
I can reproduce ~15% failures if I kill a backend pod every ~10 requests.

taylor (Eng-Runtime): that matches: upstream GOAWAY from model pod -> envoy proxies active stream closure -> client sees 502. Two vectors: (A) pod churn during streaming, (B) token rotation causing client to reuse connection while server side has partially closed state. The token length comment from Logan might matter if HPACK size causes different frame fragmentation, but that's speculative.

logan (DevEx): customer-facing mitigation options? can suggest short-term: retry logic on client side with GET-style reconnects, or route to dedicated capacity.

maria (Support): sent suggested mitigation to customer: increase client retry/backoff and disable connection reuse for short term. They pushed back — want fix from our side.

raj (Eng-SRE): immediate operator mitigations we can try: - reduce aggressive keep_alive reuse so new requests get fresh connection when backend churn is high - increase per_try_timeout on envoy so it retries other upstreams instead of failing fast - ensure GOAWAY handling is tuned so existing streams complete where possible. I can prototype a conservative change in staging.

taylor (Eng-Runtime): runtime fix ideas: - make auth middleware idempotent and tolerate token validation race during pod replace - add connection draining grace period before SIGKILL so streams have chance to finish - small change: when receiving a token header we can accept in-progress streams if they started before rotation timestamp. Need careful rollout.

maria (Support): customer also mentioned seeing a billing header injection change in their header chain (X-Redwood-Billing: acct=acct-123, tier=pro). Could that header length/format be contributing?

raj (Eng-SRE): unlikely primary cause but header size can change HPACK dynamic table behavior — in pathological cases could change fragmentation and timing. Not the main signal here.

logan (DevEx): we should give them a clear repro they can run that we can cross-check with our logs. Maria can you share a minimized repro payload and times for when they saw failures?

maria (Support): shared payload and logs with trace ids: trace-20260305-1a2b3c, trace-20260305-1a2b4d, trace-20260305-1a2b9f. Customer agrees to try turning off connection reuse (curl --no-keepalive) and report.

raj (Eng-SRE): next steps from ops: 1) test conservative envoy pool change in staging (lower keepalive reuse threshold, bump per_try_timeout), 2) monitor for regressions. I'll open PR for config and run canary.

taylor (Eng-Runtime): next steps from runtime: 1) add draining window for model pods (increase preStop sleep to allow active streams to finish), 2) code change to make auth validation tolerant during token rotation. Will scope impact and risk.

logan (DevEx): I'll draft the customer message with repro steps + suggested short-term workarounds, include we have an ops canary in progress.

maria (Support): customer acked the temporary workaround (turn off keepalive) and will test. They will also delay token rotation window to off-peak.

raj (Eng-SRE): rolling action: PR-ops-345 (envoy: lower connection reuse threshold, per_try_timeout 10s -> 15s) created and deploying to staging now. Canary target: 5% of traffic for 1h.

ops-bot: PR PR-ops-345 merged to staging at 2026-03-05T03:10:12Z. Canary started (5% traffic).

taylor (Eng-Runtime): logged runtime ticket RT-2026-78 for pod draining and auth idempotency. ETA initial patch 2026-03-12.

maria (Support): marking thread for follow-up. Will update once customer confirms. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

logan (DevEx): also slack note — if we see similar pattern across customers, escalate to infra incident. For now monitoring SLO noise.

raj (Eng-SRE): monitoring note: I'm watching 502 rate vs upstream restart rate and h2 GOAWAY count. If 502s don't fall after canary, we'll rollback.

maria (Support): last update from customer at 2026-03-05T04:00Z: disabling keepalive reduced failures from ~12% -> ~1%. They will hold off rotation for now. I'll leave this open until ops canary finishes.
